policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Upon the first day of the week' renders the idiom identically whether the noun is singular σαββάτου or plural σαββάτων; the English does not distinguish number here.
ἐὰν and ἂν with the subjunctive are the same particle orthographically; ASV 'as he may prosper' renders either without distinction.

ASV 'And when I arrive' renders ὅταν/ὅτ᾽ ἂν alike; the only ASV note here is an alternative_rendering about where 'by letters' attaches, which concerns English wording and does not bear on this particle.
Word order only: ἄξιον ᾖ and ᾖ ἄξιον both yield ASV 'if it be meet'; English word order is fixed by its own grammar and cannot distinguish the Greek sequence.
ASV 'I shall abide' translates the simple verb of remaining; παραμενῶ and καταμενῶ differ only in preverb and are both rendered 'abide' without any distinguishing English trace or note.
ASV 'or even winter' renders the adverbial καὶ with 'even'; the WH text omitting καὶ would give simply 'or winter'.
ASV 'For I do not wish to see you now by the way' renders the causal γάρ; the RP δέ would be rendered 'But'.
Aorist ἐπιτρέψῃ and present ἐπιτρέπῃ subjunctive alike appear as ASV 'if the Lord permit'; the English conditional carries no aspect marking.
ASV 'But I will tarry at Ephesus until Pentecost' is future; the WH present ἐπιμένω would be rendered 'I abide/am staying'.
ASV 'as I also do' renders the καί, which excludes the bare ἐγώ of r01; κἀγώ and καὶ ἐγώ are crasis and uncrased forms of the same words and the English cannot distinguish them.
Enclitic με and emphatic ἐμέ are both rendered ASV 'unto me'; the English marks no emphasis and no note is attached.
ASV 'that which was lacking on your part' renders possessive ὑμέτερον and genitive ὑμῶν identically; the attached note is a greek_gloss on 'presence', which does not bear on this unit.
ASV 'The churches of Asia salute you' uses a verb form identical for singular and plural subjects in English; neither ἀσπάζεται nor ἀσπάζονται leaves a distinguishing trace.
ASV reads 'Aquila and Prisca', transliterating Πρίσκα; the RP Πρίσκιλλα would give 'Priscilla'.
ASV 'If any man loveth not the Lord' has no christological expansion; the RP addition would give 'the Lord Jesus Christ'.
ASV leaves the Aramaic untransliterated as one word 'Maranatha', and its note offers both parsings ('O (or Our) Lord, come!'), so the English neither divides the phrase as Μαράνα θά nor as Μαρὰν ἀθά.
ASV 'The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you' includes Χριστοῦ, which the base text lacks.
ASV ends 'My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.', rendering the concluding Ἀμήν absent from the base text.
